proofs.fixed_future_grouping: If Sig_B(beta) is identical inside a class C, then sum_{beta in C} M_A(beta,z)M_B(beta,z)=Sig_C(z)*sum_{beta in C}M_A(beta,z).
proofs.universal_identity: For beta!=beta', choose differing x_i and literal l_i true on beta. With fresh y,z, future clause (l_i OR y OR z) has signature 4*z on beta and 1+3*z on beta'. Therefore beta and beta' are not universally future-congruent under the frozen grammar.

scoped_consequences: Formula-specific exact future signatures can merge boundary rows without changing the occupancy generating polynomial.
A formula-independent quotient valid for every allowed arbitrary future 3-CNF continuation cannot merge any two distinct boundary assignments.
Class count alone is not a complexity bound: representing or computing the beta-to-class map may still be exponential.
